prompt: Look at the sequence $2,\ 6,\ 18,\ 54,\ \dots$ What is the next term?
hint: The gaps keep growing, so try DIVIDING each term by the one before it instead.

hints.text: The gaps keep growing, so try DIVIDING each term by the one before it instead.
The ratios are $6 \div 2 = 3$, $18 \div 6 = 3$, and $54 \div 18 = 3$, so the rule multiplies by $3$. Apply it to the last term.
Multiplying once more gives $54 \times 3 = 162$, so the next term is $162$.

explanation: The jumps between terms are $4, 12, 36$, which are not equal, so the sequence is not arithmetic.
Dividing instead shows each term is $3$ times the one before, so it is GEOMETRIC with $r = 3$.
Continuing the rule from the last term gives $54 \times 3 = 162$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Arithmetic or geometric? A quick test
steps: Subtract first: 6 − 2 = 4 but 18 − 6 = 12. The gaps disagree, so it is NOT arithmetic.
Now divide: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 and 18 ÷ 6 = 3. The ratios agree, so it IS geometric.
Once the ratio is 3, the next term is 54 × 3 = 162.

alternativeExplanations.title: Write each term as powers of 3
steps: Each new term just glues on one more factor of 3.
The fifth term glues on one more: 2 × 3⁴ = 2 × 81 = 162.
